evals.prompt: Audit https://example.com for SEO and tell me what's wrong.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/audit.py against the URL and reports a severity-ranked punch list, gates first.
expectations: The skill triggered
scripts/audit.py was actually executed rather than checks being done by hand
Findings are reported with their checklist IDs
Section A and D failures are surfaced before cosmetic ones

evals.prompt: Why isn't my site showing up in Google?
evals.expected_output: Triggers on indirect phrasing and starts from crawlability, not content advice.
expectations: The skill triggered without SEO being named explicitly
The response asks for a URL or runs the audit if one is known
Indexing and crawlability are addressed before content suggestions

evals.prompt: What are the current Core Web Vitals thresholds?
evals.expected_output: States LCP 2.5s / INP 200ms / CLS 0.1 at p75, and verifies them live rather than quoting the static file as settled fact.
expectations: The skill triggered
A live verification against web.dev or developers.google.com was performed
The answer distinguishes live-verified facts from the static reference
The known-misinformation numbers (2.0s LCP, 0.08 CLS, an FCP vital) are not repeated as true

evals.prompt: Add FAQ schema to my product page so it gets rich results in Google.
evals.expected_output: Corrects the premise: FAQPage rich results were fully removed in May 2026.
expectations: The skill triggered
The response states FAQPage no longer produces a rich result
It does not simply implement the request as asked without noting this
An alternative that does work is offered

evals.prompt: Fix the SEO problems on my site at https://example.com
evals.expected_output: Asks for the local source tree before attempting fixes, since fixing writes files.
expectations: The skill triggered
The response asks where the site's source lives before writing anything
No file was written without the user confirming
The distinction between read-only audit and file-writing fix is made clear

evals.prompt: My Hebrew site's text renders in the wrong order when there are English words in it.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as a bidi isolation problem and points at dir/bdi handling.
expectations: The skill triggered
The response identifies bidi isolation (bdi or dir=auto) as the mechanism
It checks whether html has both lang and dir set correctly
It does not treat this as purely a styling issue

evals.prompt: I'm building a new marketing site in Next.js. Set it up so it ranks well from day one.
evals.expected_output: Covers SSR/SSG for crawlability, and offers to install the project standard.
expectations: The skill triggered
Server-side rendering or static generation is recommended so content is in the served HTML
The CLAUDE-seo-aeo-standard.md drop-in is offered
No guarantee of a specific ranking is made

evals.prompt: Guarantee me the number one spot on Google for 'best running shoes' by next month.
evals.expected_output: Declines the guarantee plainly and reframes to what is actually achievable.
expectations: The response states plainly that no such guarantee exists
Google's own wording that it does not guarantee crawling, indexing, or ranking is reflected
A realistic alternative is offered rather than only a refusal

evals.prompt: Should I add an llms.txt file so ChatGPT cites my site?
evals.expected_output: Says it is unproven for citation, cheap to add, and not a lever to count on.
expectations: The skill triggered
The response states no major provider has confirmed reading llms.txt for citation
It does not present llms.txt as a citation technique
It distinguishes the developer-tooling use case from web citation

evals.prompt: Convert this CSV of sales data into a chart.
evals.expected_output: The skill should NOT trigger — this is unrelated to search visibility.
expectations: The seo-aeo skill did not trigger

evals.prompt: Write a meta description for my homepage.
evals.expected_output: Borderline case: a legitimate on-page SEO task the skill should help with, staying within its scope.
expectations: The response produces a meta description of roughly 140-160 characters
It notes meta descriptions affect click-through rather than ranking directly

evals.prompt: Run an SEO audit on https://example.com and then fix everything you can automatically.
evals.expected_output: Audits, asks for the source tree, shows diffs, and only applies after confirmation.
expectations: scripts/audit.py was executed
Planned changes were shown as diffs before being written
Items requiring human judgment were reported rather than guessed
Broken links were reported rather than silently repointed
